title: Attention is a medium
description: Editorial introduction and transparent source-image provenance.
text:
PLAIN SIGHT / OBSERVATION EDITION
EDITORIAL
THE ORDINARY, OBSERVED DIFFERENTLY.
02 / 24
Nothing new.
Something
noticed.
A wall beside a seated figure. A stem connecting a dark
flower to a clear glass. A chair holding the scale of an
empty room.
The material does not change when we look again. The relationships do.
This edition moves between the whole image, its existing editorial crops
and new notes on what those edits make visible.
This is a self-directed studio concept by Jocelyn Martinez. All five original image scenes are AI-generated. The
eleven derivatives are crops, not additional photographs. No real shoot, commissioned talent, camera settings
or client results are implied.


IMAGE DESCRIPTION
Editorial introduction and transparent source-image provenance.

title: Observe. Reframe. Read.
description: Three editorial actions and the relationship between original images and derivatives.
text:
PLAIN SIGHT / OBSERVATION EDITION
METHOD
THE ORDINARY, OBSERVED DIFFERENTLY.
04 / 24
The frame
is a choice.
01
Observe
Give the whole image time. Notice where the subject sits and what the
surrounding space contributes.
02
Reframe
Place a crop beside its source. Ask what gains emphasis and what
information is lost.
03
Read
Follow the sequence. The next image can offer context, sharpen a detail or
provide a pause.

Three editorial actions and the relationship between original images and derivatives.

title: Presence, or the space beside it.
description: Two actual crops from the seated source: a close portrait and a wall-led edit.
text:
PLAIN SIGHT / OBSERVATION EDITION
GESTURES
THE ORDINARY, OBSERVED DIFFERENTLY.
07 / 24
FRAMING DECISIONS / SOURCE 01
Presence, or the space beside
it.
CROP 1 / FROM SOURCE 01
Bring the posture
forward
A square edit brings the face, hands and folded
trousers into one compact reading. It gains
intimacy and gives up the breathing room of
the original.
CROP 2 / FROM SOURCE 01
Let absence take the lead
Moving attention toward the wall makes the
figure partial. The chair edge becomes a trace
of presence; use this as a pause after the full
scene, not as a replacement portrait.
Compare both with the original: plain-sight/light-table.html?source=gesture-seated

text:
PLAIN SIGHT / OBSERVATION EDITION

THE ORDINARY, OBSERVED DIFFERENTLY.

FRAMING DECISIONS / SOURCE 02
From gesture to material.
CROP 1 / FROM SOURCE 02
Follow the turn
Removing the lower fabric directs attention to
the turn of the head and the hand at the
shoulder. The composition becomes a gesture
of attention rather than a study of the garment.
CROP 2 / FROM SOURCE 02
Read the material
Taking the face out of the frame changes the
subject to light and material. The diagonal fold
carries the eye across the edit; this detail
belongs beside its parent image.
Compare both with the original: plain-sight/light-table.html?source=gesture-fabric

title: The stem, or the weight below.
description: Two actual crops from the flower source isolate the flower-and-glass relationship and the material base.
text:

ARRANGEMENTS

13 / 24
FRAMING DECISIONS / SOURCE 03
The stem, or the weight below.
CROP 1 / FROM SOURCE 03
Keep the vertical
conversation
This tighter vertical edit keeps the flower and
water connected while removing the pedestal.
It makes the fragile stem more prominent and
the setting less important.
CROP 2 / FROM SOURCE 03
Give weight to the base
The base edit exchanges the flower for three
surfaces: glass, linen and stone. Their different
edges and textures become the subject. The
absent flower is understood through the
original.
Compare both with the original: plain-sight/light-table.html?source=arrangement-bloom

title: Weight and counterweight.
description: Two crops from the table source: the clustered objects and the lighter diagonal composition.
text:
PLAIN SIGHT / OBSERVATION EDITION
ARRANGEMENTS
THE ORDINARY, OBSERVED DIFFERENTLY.
15 / 24
FRAMING DECISIONS / SOURCE 04
Weight and counterweight.
CROP 1 / FROM SOURCE 04
Collect the visual weight
The lower, wider edit gathers the vase, glass
and fruit into a dense cluster. It strengthens
material relationships while reducing the
original's airy branch and wall.
CROP 2 / FROM SOURCE 04
Let light organize the
image
Removing the heavy vase leaves the branch and
glass suspended across the light. The diagonal
now organizes the image. Compare the quieter
balance with the clustered object edit.
Compare both with the original: plain-sight/light-table.html?source=arrangement-table

FRAMING DECISIONS / SOURCE 05
A trace of presence.
CROP 02 / CHAIR
The chair gives the room a human scale even
when no person is present. Removing the
opening concentrates the relationship
between its rigid edges and the sloping light.
CROP 03 / SHADOW
The wider floor edit connects opening and chair
through shadow. It changes a vertical room into
a horizontal sequence, useful as a closing image
after the more enclosed crops.

THE ORDINARY, OBSERVED DIFFERENTLY.
23 / 24

Look again.

Jocelyn Martinez / self-directed concept, visual identity, editorial art direction and interface
reconstruction.
IMAGE PROVENANCE
Five existing AI-generated source scenes. Eleven existing derivative crops. New authored
framing notes. No shoot, real models, camera settings, client campaign or user-study findings
are implied.
PRODUCTION
24 A4 portrait pages, 210 × 297 mm. RGB digital-review PDF; no external bleed, commercial
preflight or physical proof. Effective image resolution varies. A printer-ready edition needs
source-resolution and color-profile review.

plain-sight/src/build_publication.py. All original source images and the previous edition are
